title: fix(hooks): read a command substitution inside a double-quoted word as its own quoting context
body:
Fixes #24812

Clause-②: no

## What

`.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` read a `"` inside a `$(…)` (or a backtick) that sits inside a double-quoted word as the END of the outer string. The rest of the substitution body was then scanned as bare shell, so the `>` inside a quoted curl JSON body became a redirect and the next fragment a write "target", and a read-only command run from the primary checkout was blocked.

One helper, `subst_end()`, now answers where such a substitution ends, reading its body with its own quotes, escapes and nesting (`(…)`, `$(…)`, backticks). All three quote-aware scanners (the heredoc comment scan `strip_line_comment()`, segmentation `split_segments()`, tokenisation `tokenize()`) delegate to it from their in-double-quote branch, so they agree on the extent by construction. The body is kept verbatim as part of the word, so a target holding it still fails open on its `$`, which is the header's existing promise for `$(…)` targets.

Diff: 2 files, +77 / -1 (`.claude/**` only, Tier S).

## Approach: why the substitution is tracked rather than failed open

The card offers two routes, and the dispatch preferred failing open on any double-quoted word containing `$(` for its smaller parser surface. I measured what that route gives up before choosing. The hook cannot know where an unreadable word ends, so failing open on it means claiming nothing from that segment onward. On the pre-fix hook these three writes into the primary checkout are all blocked, correctly, and that route would let all three through: `sed -i "s/a/$(date +%F)/" pkg/x.ts` (the reflexive in-place edit this guard exists for), `X="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" ; sed -i s/a/b/ pkg/x.ts` (any write behind a quoted-substitution preamble), and `echo "$(date)" > pkg/x.ts`. Tracking the substitution costs one ~30-line helper that answers a single question (where the body ends) and never classifies anything. It is called from all three scanners' existing in-quote branch, so the passes cannot drift apart on it. Measured against the pre-fix hook, it never reads a command worse, with one exception: a `(` or `)` that bash would not count (a `case` pattern, a comment inside the substitution) moves the end. Too early, and the rest is read exactly as before. Too late, and the swallowed text is inert, i.e. fails open. That boundary is written in the helper's header. The selftest pins the recall boundary in both directions (the three writes above stay blocked), so the alternative route would go red on it.

## Measurement (cwd = primary checkout; payload `{"tool_input":{"command":…},"cwd":"/home/user/objectstack"}`)

| command | pre-fix `b1676441b` | this PR `e4ba00dc9` |
|---|---|---|
| `echo "a $(curl -d "{\"c\":\"x > 1\"}" http://h)"` | 2, `target: 1"` | 0 |
| `echo "a $(curl -d '{"c":"x > 1"}' http://h)"` | 2, `target: 1}' http://h)` | 0 |
| `curl -s -d "{\"c\":\"x > 1\"}" http://h` | 0 | 0 |
| control `echo hi > out.txt` | 2, `target: out.txt` | 2, `target: out.txt` |
| original probe `echo "PUT $1 -> $(curl … -d "{…\"condition\":\"int(record.title) > 1\"…}" …)"` | 2, `target: 1"` | 0 |
| backtick spelling of row 1 | 2, `target: 1"` | 0 |
| `echo "$(date)" > /home/user/objectstack/f` | 2 | 2 |
| `X="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" && echo "$X" > /home/user/objectstack/f` | 2 | 2 |

**H2 (both passes share the defect): confirmed by per-site ablation.** Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode at `0963684e5`: one call site replaced by a no-op, the hook self-test run as the child, then a restore proven by blob equality with HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Results:

- segmentation only reverted: 3 red (card form 1, the backtick form, the fail-open mirror);
- tokenisation only reverted: 2 red (both card forms);
- heredoc comment scan only reverted: 1 red (the heredoc pin);
- the helper's nested-`$(` arm removed: 1 red (the nested pin).

So no single pass fixes it alone. The whole pre-fix hook (`b1676441b`, blob `1fd91d0a8`) against the new self-test: 136 passed, 5 failed. The 5 are both card forms, the backtick form, the fail-open mirror and the heredoc pin.

The first A2/A3 attempts were refused by the tool itself, not run: a bare `:` replacement collided with the `:` already in the anchor. They were re-run with unique markers. `e4ba00dc9` after the ablations is comment-only.

**H3 (a real redirect inside a quoted `$(…)`).** Pre-fix: `echo "$(cat x > /home/user/objectstack/f)"` exit 0, and `x="$(sed -i s/a/b/ /home/user/objectstack/README.md)"` exit 0. The write sat inside the string, by accident of the quote reading. After: the same, exit 0. The answer is unchanged, but it is now a deliberate fail-open, listed among the wrapped invocations in the header and pinned in the self-test's "deliberately NOT claim" section. The UNQUOTED `echo $(cat x > /home/user/objectstack/f)` is still blocked (exit 2), unchanged.

## Tests and gates, all at HEAD `e4ba00dc9`

- `bash .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.selftest.sh`: `141 passed, 0 failed` (130 on `main`; +11 cases).
- The other hook matrices in `.claude/hooks/`: `guard-main-checkout` 120/0, `guard-process-kill` 69/0, `guard-shared-stash` 53/0 and `guard-tree-enum` 38/0.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 16 families. All 16 ran with exit 0, captured before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: `16 derived, 16 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.
- `pnpm check:bash32-floor` reports `19 constructs checked, floor bash 3.2`. The helper uses only `${s:i:n}`, `+=`, `${st%?}` and arithmetic `for`. There is no recursion, no `mapfile` and no negative substring offset.
- `check:doc-formula-expressions` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` (exit 3, unbuilt `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint`). I built both under the verify lock and re-ran it: exit 0.
- Also run: `pnpm check:pm-settings-deny-roster` (its roster lives under `.claude`): exit 0.
- No changeset: `.claude/**` publishes nothing (`skip-changeset`).

## Acceptance notes

- **Same defect in the sibling stash guard (not touched: outside this card's declared file surface).** `.claude/hooks/guard-shared-stash.sh` `split_segments()` carries the identical in-quote branch. `echo "a $(echo "x; git stash pop")"` is a pure read, yet the guard answers exit 2 (blocked); `echo "x; git stash pop"` answers 0. Measured at `b1676441b`. The fix there is a ~3-line delegation to the same helper shape; reported to the seat for a family card.
- **The objectui twins carry it too.** objectui `9eb1479`, `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`: both card forms exit 2. objectui `guard-shared-stash.sh`: the stash shape above exits 2. This hook's header says the two repos' copies are kept case-for-case identical, so this PR opens a mirror obligation there. Reported, not filed.
- **Neighbouring shape, not this card:** a parameter expansion with a nested quote inside a double-quoted word, `echo "${x:-"a > b"}"`, is still blocked (exit 2, `target: b}`). Its single-quote semantics differ from `$(…)` (a `'` inside `"${…}"` is literal), so it is not a mechanical extension of this helper. Reported to the seat.
- Cost: on a 2.5 KB, 25-line command of the card's probe shape, the hook takes 247 ms. The pre-fix hook took 158 ms, but it stopped at the false block on line 1, so the two numbers do not measure the same work.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

### 改了什么
修了 Bash 写保护钩子的一个误判。命令里如果有双引号包着的 `$(…)`(或反引号),而这段子命令里又带了引号,钩子会把内层引号当成外层字符串的结束,结果把 JSON 里的 `>` 当成重定向,拦下了根本不写文件的只读命令。现在由一个公共函数判断子命令到哪里结束,三处扫描都改用它,判断结果一致。

### 为什么改
云端会话里每次命令都在主检出目录下执行。开发 agent 用 curl 发带 `>` 条件的 JSON 探测请求时被误拦,只能把请求挪进临时脚本绕开。钩子头部自己承诺过:看不懂的形状一律放行,绝不误拦只读命令;这次的误拦违背了这个承诺。

### 风险与代价(含回滚)
钩子多了约 30 行、只负责找子命令结尾的函数。没有选「遇到就整体放行」的方案,因为实测那样会漏放 `sed -i "s/a/$(date)/" 文件` 这类真正写进主检出的命令。已知边界:子命令内部有 `case` 分支或带括号的注释时,结尾判断可能偏移;偏早就退回旧行为,偏晚则放行(不误拦)。回滚就是 revert 本 PR,只涉及两个 `.claude/hooks` 文件。

### 席位意见


### 你要做的
无需操作:这是 Tier S,席位按契约档复核后自行落地。另外,objectui 的两个同名钩子和本仓的 `guard-shared-stash.sh` 有同一个缺陷,已在报告里交席位跟进。
